facts.subject: body:steel
facts.value: Water containing road salt accelerates body-steel corrosion.
facts.notes: Factory description of basic corrosion mechanism, not an incidence or repairability statistic.

facts.subject: body:corrosion_protection
facts.value: Body steel is protected by several coats of paint; large areas are zinc-coated.
facts.notes: Not proof of present coating condition or immunity to rust.

facts.subject: body:mounting_geometry
facts.value: Powertrain-subframe attachment points and body apertures must remain in their correct geometric positions.
facts.notes: Dimensions and their measurement procedure require the linked Body dimensions section.

facts.subject: body:repair
facts.value: For serious body-member deformation Saab calls for an alignment bench and diagonal measurement.
facts.notes: Cannot determine safe structural condition by appearance alone.

facts.subject: body:front_subframe_mount
facts.value: Rear nut piece of front subframe is serviced via floor interior and an access hole; anti-corrosion treatment is part of closure.
facts.notes: Identifies a structural fastening zone, not a known-frequency rust defect.

facts.subject: body:rear_subframe_mount
facts.value: Rear subframe nut piece can be accessed through interior floor opening; access edge receives anti-corrosion treatment and plug.
facts.notes: The WIS page does not establish corrosion frequency or a universal physical rear-subframe replacement recommendation.

facts.subject: body:rear_sill
facts.value: Rear sill panel procedure requires inspection of the underlying reinforcement and replacement if damaged.
facts.notes: Prescribed factory repair; not a claim that the sill commonly fails from rust.

facts.subject: body:rear_wheelhouse
facts.value: Rear outer wheel-housing procedure includes removal and restoration of reinforcement at sill and protective seam/cavity treatment.
facts.notes: Damage severity and repairs must be evaluated in context.

facts.subject: body:rear_frame_member
facts.value: Rear frame-member section may be cut/joined only behind the specified marking; beyond that boundary, the entire member must be replaced.
facts.notes: A safety-critical repair limitation. Actual damage boundary requires the original illustration and qualified assessment.

facts.subject: body:lower_a_pillar
facts.value: Where factory MIG brazing is used, WIS forbids substitution with conventional welding and normal filler because of collision-performance concerns.
facts.notes: Source says certain joints/cars use MIG brazing. Do not assume every A-pillar joint is brazed.

facts.subject: body:front_wheelhouse
facts.value: Repair of the front wheel-housing reinforcement specifies alignment, approved welding methods and post-repair surface protection.
facts.notes: Do not generalize to all crash or rust repairs.

facts.subject: body:sedan_rear_floor
facts.value: Sedan rear-floor section repair specifies an alignment bench, welding to members and reinstatement of protective coatings.

facts.subject: body:front_lift
facts.value: Saab describes a front lifting/attachment point centered under the front subframe at the front towing-eye mounting.
facts.notes: Must use complete original illustration and suitable equipment; do not lift at a corroded or damaged point.

facts.subject: body:side_lift
facts.value: Saab identifies side jack brackets beneath the scuff members as lifting/attachment points.
facts.notes: Refer to illustration, jack stands and appropriate vehicle support; inspect mount integrity.

facts.subject: body:rear_lift
facts.value: Saab identifies rear towing-eye/towbar location, and explicitly prohibits lifting at the spare-wheel well or rear axle.
facts.notes: Factory warning is equipment/position specific; verify fitment and condition before lifting.

facts.subject: body:body_repair
facts.value: Specified structural-panel repairs restore primer, seam sealant, and cavity corrosion protection after welding and painting.
facts.notes: No general-purpose coating guarantees lasting repair of rusted load-bearing material.

parts.title: Floor access closure plug for subframe nut-piece repair
requirements: Specific WIS access-hole repair is required; no unverified interchange with other plugs.
Verify actual part identity, supply and exact repair procedure before ordering.
parts.notes: Factory WIS mentions plug by part number in nut-piece repair instructions; no catalog supersession or live orderability checked.

gaps.title: Year-by-year structural applicability
missing_inputs: Retrieve body and corrosion repair sections for MY2004–2009 and verify revisions independently.
gaps.reason: MY2006 WIS entry proves the described procedure, not unchanged application across model years.

gaps.title: Quantified rust acceptance and safety criteria
missing_inputs: Obtain jurisdictional inspection requirements and manufacturer-approved corrosion damage rejection criteria, if published; acquire measurements/photos for each real car.
gaps.reason: These repair procedures do not provide a universal corrosion depth or structural integrity threshold.

gaps.title: Front and rear subframe assembly identities
missing_inputs: Get EPC assemblies, fastening revisions, steel specifications, mount drawings and differences between sedan/wagon and drivetrain options.
gaps.reason: Nut-piece procedures and structural attachment locations cannot certify replacement subframe fitment.

gaps.title: Corrosion-focused inspection zone survey
missing_inputs: Expand documented factory inspection paths for jacking points, seams, rear spring attachment areas, brake/fuel lines and enclosed cavities.
gaps.reason: Factory repairability and salt mechanism are not evidence of actual frequency or extent in used northeastern US examples.

gaps.title: Repair scope and professional capability
missing_inputs: Obtain current approved structural repair methods, measuring fixtures, qualified workshop costs and part availability for a chosen car.
gaps.reason: Documenting a WIS welding procedure does not make it safely DIY-executable or economical.
